explanation: Store normalized BigInt credits in a map and a randomized treap ordered by (credit,id). AddAll changes a common offset. Replacing a client removes its old treap entry before inserting its new normalized value.
timeComplexity: Insert/Remove/Max: expected O(log n), O(n) worst case if the randomized treap degenerates. Lookup: expected O(1); AddAll: O(1), treating BigInt arithmetic as constant for bounded credits. The operation bounds reflect the displayed index: ordered set, randomized treap, or a Python scan for Max.
spaceComplexity: O(n) storage; recursive treap operations use expected O(log n), worst-case O(n) stack. The client dictionary and any ranking index contain one entry per live client.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The map and treap contain exactly the same clients and normalized credits. Treap rotations preserve key order, and priorities preserve the heap condition. A common offset preserves all credit comparisons, so the rightmost treap key is a maximum-credit client.
walkthrough: Insert client Nora with credit 4, then AddAll(6): Lookup(Nora) is 10. Reinsert Nora with credit 3, which replaces its absolute credit. Max is Nora; after removal Lookup is −1 and Max is empty. JSON arguments are [operations], with each operation [name,stringArg,intArg]. lookup/remove/max records carry expected observations, not extra callable parameters. Observed true means all operations validated.
edgeCases: Reinsertion replaces an absolute credit, even after AddAll.
Tied maximum credits are broken by client ID here, but the mathematical contract permits any tied client.
A new instance resets the map, tree, and offset.
The judge maintains expected credits independently and accepts any existing client with the maximum credit. No universal tie-breaker is required.
